# source: conformance/scenarios/characters.txt

scenario characters/bracket-range
kind normative
spec The range notation, e.g. [a-zA-Z], can be used to match one of the characters in a range.
file .gitignore
| file[0-9].txt
| [a-c]x
path file0.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:file[0-9].txt
path file9.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:file[0-9].txt
path filea.txt => NONE
path file10.txt => NONE
path file.txt => NONE
path ax => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:[a-c]x
path cx => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:[a-c]x
path dx => NONE
path dir/bx => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:[a-c]x

scenario characters/bracket-set-and-negation
kind normative
spec A bracket expression matches one of the listed characters; "!" or "^" right after the opening bracket negates it.
file .gitignore
| a[xyz]
| b[!xyz]
| c[^xyz]
path ax => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[xyz]
path az => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[xyz]
path aw => NONE
path bw => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:b[!xyz]
path bx => NONE
path cw => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:c[^xyz]
path cx => NONE
path c/ => NONE

scenario characters/bracket-does-not-match-slash
kind normative
spec Wildcards in git match with the pathname flag, so a bracket expression never matches a slash.
file .gitignore
| a[!x]b
| c[^x]d
path a-b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[!x]b
path a/b => NONE
path c-d => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c[^x]d
path c/d => NONE

scenario characters/bracket-close-first
kind git-quirk
spec Behavior follows fnmatch(3) as used by Git's wildmatch.
note A closing bracket directly after the opening bracket or after the negation is a literal member of the set.
file .gitignore
| a[]]b
| c[!]]d
path a]b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[]]b
path ab => NONE
path a[b => NONE
path c-d => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c[!]]d
path c]d => NONE

scenario characters/bracket-literal-dash
kind git-quirk
spec Behavior follows fnmatch(3) as used by Git's wildmatch.
note A dash first or last in a set is literal.
file .gitignore
| a[-x]
| b[x-]
| c[a-]
path a- => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[-x]
path ax => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[-x]
path ay => NONE
path b- => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:b[x-]
path bx => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:b[x-]
path c- => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:c[a-]
path ca => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:c[a-]

scenario characters/bracket-reversed-range
kind git-quirk
spec A range whose end precedes its start is not described by gitignore(5).
note Observed behavior of Git, kept to document the behavior.
file .gitignore
| a[z-a]
path az => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[z-a]
path aa => NONE
path am => NONE

scenario characters/bracket-character-classes
kind normative
spec The pattern syntax of fnmatch(3) is used, including POSIX character classes such as [[:alpha:]].
file .gitignore
| a[[:digit:]]
| b[[:upper:]]
| c[[:alpha:][:digit:]]
| d[[:space:]]
| e[![:alnum:]]
path a5 => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[[:digit:]]
path aa => NONE
path bA => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:b[[:upper:]]
path bb => NONE
path cx => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:c[[:alpha:][:digit:]]
path c5 => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:c[[:alpha:][:digit:]]
path c- => NONE
path d`s => IGNORED # .gitignore:4:d[[:space:]]
path dx => NONE
path e- => IGNORED # .gitignore:5:e[![:alnum:]]
path ex => NONE
path e5 => NONE

scenario characters/bracket-unknown-class
kind git-quirk
spec An unknown POSIX class name is not described by gitignore(5).
note Git treats the whole pattern as non-matching when a class name is unknown.
file .gitignore
| a[[:nosuch:]]
| b[[:digit:]]
path a1 => NONE
path anosuch => NONE
path b1 => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:b[[:digit:]]

scenario characters/bracket-unterminated
kind git-quirk
spec Unterminated bracket expressions are not described by gitignore(5).
note Git never matches a pattern whose bracket expression is not closed.
file .gitignore
| a[bc
| [
| x[
path a[bc => NONE
path ab => NONE
path [ => NONE
path x[ => NONE
path x => NONE

scenario characters/bracket-with-escape
kind normative
spec A backslash escapes the next character, including inside a bracket expression.
file .gitignore
| a[\]]b
| c[\-x]
path a]b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a[\]]b
path ab => NONE
path a\b => NONE
path c- => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c[\-x]
path cx => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c[\-x]
path c\ => NONE

scenario characters/escaped-wildcards
kind normative
spec A backslash makes the following wildcard character an ordinary character.
file .gitignore
| a\*b
| c\?d
| e\[f\]
path a*b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a\*b
path aXb => NONE
path c?d => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c\?d
path cXd => NONE
path e[f] => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:e\[f\]
path eXf => NONE

scenario characters/escaped-ordinary-character
kind normative
spec A backslash in front of an ordinary character yields that character.
file .gitignore
| \a\b\c
| d\.txt
path abc => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:\a\b\c
path d.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:d\.txt
path \a\b\c => NONE
path a\b\c => NONE

scenario characters/escaped-backslash
kind normative
spec A doubled backslash matches one literal backslash.
file .gitignore
| a\\b
| c\\*
path a\b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a\\b
path ab => NONE
path a\\b => NONE
path c\ => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c\\*
path c\x => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c\\*
path cx => NONE

scenario characters/trailing-backslash
kind normative
spec A pattern that ends in an unescaped backslash is invalid and never matches.
file .gitignore
| abc\
| def\\
path abc => NONE
path abc\ => NONE
path def\\ => NONE
path def\ => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:def\\
path def => NONE

scenario characters/escaped-slash-and-space
kind git-quirk
spec Escapes in front of a separator are not described by gitignore(5).
note Git matches the pattern text verbatim, so an escaped slash behaves like a literal path separator in the pattern.
file .gitignore
| a\/b
| c\ d
path a/b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a\/b
path c`sd => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c\ d
path c`sd/x => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c\ d

scenario characters/hash-and-leading-special
kind normative
spec A line starting with # serves as a comment. Put a backslash in front of the first hash for patterns that begin with a hash.
file .gitignore
| \#notcomment
| #comment
| a#b
path #notcomment => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:\#notcomment
path comment => NONE
path #comment => NONE
path a#b => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:a#b
path notcomment => NONE

scenario characters/regex-metacharacters-are-literal
kind normative
spec Only *, ?, [ and the backslash are special; other characters match themselves.
file .gitignore
| a.b
| c+d
| (e)
| f{1,2}
| g|h
| i^j
| k$l
| m%n
path a.b => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:a.b
path axb => NONE
path c+d => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:c+d
path ccd => NONE
path (e) => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:(e)
path e => NONE
path f{1,2} => IGNORED # .gitignore:4:f{1,2}
path ff => NONE
path g|h => IGNORED # .gitignore:5:g|h
path g => NONE
path i^j => IGNORED # .gitignore:6:i^j
path k$l => IGNORED # .gitignore:7:k$l
path m%n => IGNORED # .gitignore:8:m%n

scenario characters/names-with-spaces
kind normative
spec Trailing spaces are ignored unless they are quoted with backslash; spaces inside a pattern are literal.
file .gitignore
| my file.txt
| two  spaces
| tab`there
path my`sfile.txt => IGNORED # .gitignore:1:my file.txt
path myfile.txt => NONE
path two`s`sspaces => IGNORED # .gitignore:2:two  spaces
path two`sspaces => NONE
path tab`there => IGNORED # .gitignore:3:tab`there
path tabthere => NONE

scenario characters/leading-space
kind normative
spec Leading spaces are significant.
file .gitignore
|  leading
path `sleading => IGNORED # .gitignore:1: leading
path leading => NONE
